standingCriteria: Location: remote is a hard filter, no exceptions, including hybrid. OR local to St. Cloud/Collegeville MN.
Duration: needs to fit around one semester. A posting tagged "Internship" is not automatically semester-length, check for hidden 12/18/24-month commitments (see dealbreaker checklist).

Hours: internship/part-time/full-time are all technically fine, but he strongly prefers ≤~15 hrs/week. Confirmed full-time (~40 hrs/wk) is a hard no as of 2026-08-11 ("if its 40hr a week i cant do that"), don't apply to those even if otherwise a great fit.
Pay matters, best pay prioritized. Any real pay structure (hourly, monthly stipend) is fine, just needs to be a real, stated number.
Excludes pure BD/sales roles, even when blended into a "marketing" title (cold-call quotas, outbound-outreach-heavy duties).
Skill fit: content creation, social media, brand marketing, Chinese/overseas social media (Weibo, KOL/creator outreach, this is his real JCM International experience and a strong differentiator).

dealbreakers.intro: Learned the hard way across two full verification passes (2026-08-11/12). Open the full posting body and, if the body is silent on something, check the actual application form before trusting a platform tag:
items: Region-locked "remote." "Remote" can mean remote-within-one-country-only ("work from anywhere in India," "PAN India," tied to one city with no "worldwide" language).
Ambiguous or absent pay. "Unpaid / Paid" both listed, or no figure anywhere in the body.
Fixed live-meeting hours in the wrong timezone. Convert to Central before judging fit.
"Remote" tag contradicted by the body (says On-site/Hybrid instead).

"Internship" tag can also lie, on hours AND duration. Confirmed real case (90 Seconds, 2026-08-12): posting said nothing about hours or duration, tagged "Internship," but the application form itself asked for a 12/18/24-month commitment. If the body is silent, don't assume semester-length or part-time, flag as unconfirmed.
BD/sales role wearing a marketing title. Cold-call quotas, outbound quota language.

Eligibility mismatches. Graduates-only (excludes him, still enrolled), "based in [country]" residency requirements, required fluency in a language he doesn't speak (he has English native, Mandarin/Japanese conversational, not French/German/etc. at professional level).
Closed or expired applications, even if the search result looked current.
Recruiter-agency postings speaking "on behalf of our client" with no named employer, especially if the same template is reused across multiple listings, low-trust pattern.
